newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close slightly lower on rate worries.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close slightly lower on rate worries.

text.p: French stocks faded at session end to close slightly lower as questions about the direction of interest rates in Europe weighed on markets.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 0.98 points or 0.05 percent at 2124.76 after spending nearly the entire day in positive territory. CAC-40 futures were down 12 points.

The index did not benefit from a small rise in U.S. stocks after U.S. third-quarter gross domestic product growth rose 2.2 percent after second-quarter growth of 4.7 percent. U.S. debt markets lost ground near the end of the day, which added another negative factor for French shares.
Volume was 4.8 billion francs of which 3.2 billion francs on CAC-40 shares.

The surprise 25 basis point rate increase in Britain pushed the FTSE 100 index lower and combined with comments earlier in the week on German interest rates produced some caution on the part of investors, traders said.
Predictions from U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs that the U.S. Federal Reserve would raise rates by 125 basis points in the next 12 to 18 months also prompted some fears.
It was the third consecutive drop for Paris shares which have come back to their levels of the beginning of October.
Many dealers said they expected the bourse to drop again on Thursday. The bourse is closed Friday for All Saints Day.
* Peugeot was the biggest loser on the day, down 4.29 percent on worries about medium term outlook now that the government car buying incentive programme has ended.

* LVMH rose 3.41 percent on news it would spend 12.6 billion francs to take control of U.S. based duty free chain DFS. LVMH shrugged off an announcement that S&P put LVMH short term paper on watch with negative implications.
* Dior shares, lifted by LVMH rise, end up 3.35 percent.
* Lagardere closed up 2.98 percent on belief it will win the bidding for Thomson despite public outcry over government decision.
* Sidel closed 3.98 percent higher, the day's biggest gainer on higher nine-month sales and brighter profit outlook.
* Legris up 3.85 percent after several brokers lifted their ratings on the company.
